verdict.rationale: LightSprint's pricing page claims it can run in your own infrastructure or private cloud, which is a first-party self-hosting option for the product's agent infrastructure. It is a single marketing-level line with no deployment documentation. Local coding via Claude or Codex is a third-party workaround, not LightSprint self-hosting, so it earns no credit. Missing for 10: documented local, container (Docker/Kubernetes) or VM deployment methods, installation and operations docs, clarity on tier and availability, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can self-host agent infrastructure locally, in containers, or on my own VMs

citations.quote: Run LightSprint in your own infrastructure or private cloud environment to fit stricter security and network requirements.
